t:
Section 313 of the National Aeronautics and Space Act of 1958 (42 U.S.C. 2459f) is amended—
    (1) by amending subsection (a) to read as follows:“(a)(1) Appropriations for the Administration for fiscal year 2007 and thereafter shall be made in three accounts, ‘Science, Aeronautics, and Education’, ‘Exploration Systems and Space Operations’, and an account for amounts appropriated for the necessary expenses of the Office of the Inspector General.“(2) Within the Exploration Systems and Space Operations account, no more than 10 percent of the funds for a fiscal year for Exploration Systems may be reprogrammed for Space Operations, and no more than 10 percent of the funds for a fiscal year for Space Operations may be reprogrammed for Exploration Systems. This paragraph shall not apply to reprogramming for the purposes described in subsection (b)(2).“(3) Appropriations shall remain available for two fiscal years, unless otherwise specified in law. Each account shall include the planned full costs of Administration activities.”; and 
    (2) in subsection (b)—
        (A) by inserting “(1)” before “To ensure”; and 
        (B) by adding at the end the following new paragraph:“(2) The Administration may also transfer amounts among accounts for the immediate costs of recovering from damage caused by a major disaster (as defined in section 102 of the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act (42 U.S.C. 5122)) or by an act of terrorism, or for the immediate costs associated with an emergency rescue of astronauts.”.

fable.w: This section only restructures NASA's appropriations accounts, caps reprogramming between them, and authorizes transfers for disaster recovery or astronaut rescue. The tempting reading is that reprogramming or transfer authority implies some consultation, but no party outside the federal government is consulted, heard, or given any right to object or sue. It is purely internal federal budget management with no rulemaking, hearing, advisory body, or outside consultation.
fable.s: Appropriations for the Administration for fiscal year 2007 and thereafter shall be made in three accounts

qwen_block.w: This section details the internal accounting and appropriation structures for NASA, specifically how funds are divided into accounts and the rules for reprogramming or transferring those funds. It does not involve consultation, coordination, or participation with any entities outside the federal government (such as states, tribes, the public, or private companies). The actors involved are solely federal agencies and officials.
qwen_block.s: Appropriations for the Administration for fiscal year 2007 and thereafter shall be made in three accounts, ‘Science, Aeronautics, and Education’, ‘Exploration Systems and Space Operations’, and an account for amounts appropriated for the necessary expenses of the Office of the Inspector General.

opus.w: This section sets up NASA's appropriations accounts, limits how much money can be shifted between them, and allows transfers between accounts for disasters or astronaut rescues. Every actor involved is inside the federal government, and no state, expert, company, or member of the public takes part in any decision. The disaster-transfer language may look like it involves outside events, but it only lets NASA move its own funds internally.
opus.s: The Administration may also transfer amounts among accounts for the immediate costs of recovering from damage caused by a major disaster
opus.b: This section is only about how NASA's budget is organized. A tempting misreading would be to find participation in the reference to transfers or in the mention of "major disaster" and "act of terrorism." But these only allow NASA to move money between its own accounts. No outside party is consulted, given a say, or given a right to object or sue.

qwen_chat.w: This section outlines internal budgetary procedures and fund transfer authorities for the NASA Administration. It does not require or recommend consultation with any non-federal entities such as states, tribes, the public, or private organizations. All actors mentioned (the Administration, Congress) are inside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: Appropriations for the Administration for fiscal year 2007 and thereafter shall be made in three accounts... The Administration may also transfer amounts among accounts for the immediate costs of recovering from damage caused by a major disaster... or by an act of terrorism, or for the immediate costs associated with an emergency rescue of astronauts.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "reprogramming" or "transferring" funds involves some form of consultation or approval process that could involve outside parties. However, the text only describes the internal accounting rules and authorities of the NASA Administration (a federal agency). There is no mention of consulting with states, the public, or other non-federal entities. The actors involved are entirely within the federal government (NASA, Congress via appropriations).
